item.text:
{
  "schema_version": "evidence_intent_extraction_v1",
  "source_id": "MAC-010",
  "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
  "draft_intents": [
    {
      "draft_id": "D0001",
      "locator": "page 50",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00001",
      "actor": "Mexico's public sector",
      "action": "recorded and projected total revenue",
      "mechanism": "public-sector revenue collection",
      "outcome": "Revenue was 23.6 percent of GDP in 2019, 24.2 percent in 2020, 23.3 percent in 2021, and 24.3 percent in 2022; IMF staff projected 24.1 percent in 2023 and a gradual decline to 23.9 percent in 2025-2027.",
      "dates": "2019-2027; 2022-2027 values include projections as indicated by the table",
      "quantities": "23.6%, 24.2%, 23.3%, 24.3%, 24.1%, 24.0%, 23.9%, 23.9%, and 23.9% of GDP",
      "attribution": "Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and IMF staff estimates and projections",
      "period_fit": "The 2022 observation directly fits the target year; surrounding years provide fiscal context and later values are projections.",
      "limitations": "The table excludes state and local governments and includes state-owned enterprises and public development banks.",
      "polarity": "mixed_neutral",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0002",
      "locator": "page 50",
      "start_segment_id": "S00002",
      "end_segment_id": "S00003",
      "actor": "Mexico's public sector",
      "action": "collected taxes across income, consumption, trade, and other tax categories",
      "mechanism": "tax system",
      "outcome": "Total tax revenue was 13.6 percent of GDP in 2022, unchanged from 2021 and above 13.1 percent in 2019; income, profit, and capital-gains taxes rose to 7.9 percent of GDP in 2022, while goods-and-services taxes fell to 5.2 percent and excises fell to 0.8 percent.",
      "dates": "2019-2022, with projections through 2027",
      "quantities": "2022: total taxes 13.6%, income/profit/capital-gains taxes 7.9%, goods-and-services taxes 5.2%, VAT 4.4%, excises 0.8%, international-trade taxes 0.3%, and other taxes 0.3% of GDP",
      "attribution": "Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and IMF staff estimates and projections",
      "period_fit": "Directly describes the target-year tax structure and its recent trajectory.",
      "limitations": "Aggregate tax categories do not establish actual incidence across income classes, regions, genders, or other groups; later values are projections.",
      "polarity": "mixed_neutral",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.8"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0003",
      "locator": "page 50",
      "start_segment_id": "S00005",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007",
      "actor": "Mexico's public sector",
      "action": "executed expenditure, subsidies, transfers, social benefits, and acquisition of nonfinancial assets",
      "mechanism": "public budget",
      "outcome": "Total expenditure reached 28.0 percent of GDP in 2022. Subsidies and transfers were 2.8 percent, including a fuel subsidy of 0.5 percent; social benefits were 4.1 percent; and net acquisition of nonfinancial assets was 2.3 percent.",
      "dates": "2019-2022, with projections through 2027",
      "quantities": "2022: total expenditure 28.0%, expense 25.8%, employee compensation 3.3%, goods and services 3.2%, interest 4.7%, subsidies and transfers 2.8%, fuel subsidy 0.5%, grants 7.9%, social benefits 4.1%, and net acquisition of nonfinancial assets 2.3% of GDP",
      "attribution": "Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and IMF staff estimates and projections",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year budget evidence.",
      "limitations": "The aggregates do not show beneficiary targeting, project quality, procurement integrity, implementation timeliness, or distributional incidence; the nonfinancial-assets category is adjusted and differs from official physical-capital spending data.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0004",
      "locator": "page 50",
      "start_segment_id": "S00008",
      "end_segment_id": "S00012",
      "actor": "Mexico's public sector",
      "action": "ran fiscal deficits while maintaining a positive primary balance in 2022",
      "mechanism": "fiscal operations and public borrowing",
      "outcome": "The overall fiscal balance was negative 3.8 percent of GDP in 2022, the structural fiscal balance was negative 3.7 percent, and the primary balance was positive 0.7 percent. Gross public-sector debt was 56.2 percent of GDP and net public-sector debt was 48.5 percent.",
      "dates": "2022, with historical observations from 2019 and projections through 2027",
      "quantities": "2022 overall balance -3.8%, structural balance -3.7%, primary balance 0.7%, structural primary balance 0.7%, gross debt 56.2%, and net debt 48.5% of GDP",
      "attribution": "Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and IMF staff estimates and projections",
      "period_fit": "Directly measures target-year fiscal and debt conditions.",
      "limitations": "Structural estimates adjust revenue for economic and oil-price cycles and exclude one-off items; debt measures cover public-sector borrowing requirements under the report's definitions and do not by themselves establish policy causality or long-run sustainability.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0005",
      "locator": "page 51",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004",
      "actor": "Mexico's external sector",
      "action": "recorded a projected current-account and merchandise-trade deficit amid high trade flows and remittance income",
      "mechanism": "international trade, primary income, services, and secondary-income flows",
      "outcome": "For 2022, the report projected a current-account deficit of US$17.3 billion and a merchandise-trade deficit of US$27.4 billion, with exports of US$564.1 billion, imports of US$591.5 billion, and net secondary income, mostly remittances, of US$55.1 billion.",
      "dates": "2022 projection, with 2019-2027 series",
      "quantities": "2022: current account -US$17.3 billion; merchandise trade -US$27.4 billion; exports US$564.1 billion; manufactures exports US$488.0 billion; imports US$591.5 billion; secondary income US$55.1 billion",
      "attribution": "Bank of Mexico, National Institute of Statistics and Geography, and IMF staff estimates",
      "period_fit": "Target-year projection relevant to economic trajectory and exposure to external conditions.",
      "limitations": "A macroeconomic balance-of-payments projection does not identify the ruler's specific contribution or distributional consequences.",
      "polarity": "mixed_neutral",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.4", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0006",
      "locator": "page 52",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005",
      "actor": "Mexico's external sector",
      "action": "recorded projected external balances relative to GDP",
      "mechanism": "trade, income, remittance, and financial-account flows",
      "outcome": "The 2022 current-account deficit was projected at 1.2 percent of GDP, the merchandise-trade deficit at 1.9 percent, net secondary income at 3.8 percent, and net foreign direct investment at negative 2.1 percent under the report's balance-of-payments sign convention.",
      "dates": "2022 projection, with 2019-2027 series",
      "quantities": "2022: current account -1.2%, merchandise trade -1.9%, exports 39.1%, manufactures exports 33.8%, imports 41.0%, secondary income 3.8%, financial account -1.2%, and net FDI -2.1% of GDP",
      "attribution": "Bank of Mexico, National Institute of Statistics and Geography, and IMF staff estimates",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year external-sector context.",
      "limitations": "Projected aggregate flows do not demonstrate whether policies were fairly administered or causally responsible for investment outcomes.",
      "polarity": "mixed_neutral",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.4", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0007",
      "locator": "page 53",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00006",
      "actor": "Mexico's banking sector",
      "action": "maintained capital, asset-quality, profitability, and liquidity indicators through the second quarter of 2022",
      "mechanism": "bank capitalization, provisioning, earnings, and liquid-asset buffers",
      "outcome": "At 2022Q2, regulatory capital was 18.7 percent of risk-weighted assets, nonperforming loans were 2.3 percent of gross loans, provisions equaled 143.4 percent of nonperforming loans, return on equity was 17.4 percent, and liquid assets equaled 38.5 percent of short-term liabilities and 49.8 percent of total assets.",
      "dates": "2022Q2, compared with annual data for 2016-2021",
      "quantities": "18.7% regulatory capital ratio; 17.3% Tier 1 ratio; 2.3% NPL ratio; 143.4% provisions-to-NPL ratio; 17.4% return on equity; 38.5% liquid assets to short-term liabilities; 49.8% liquid assets to total assets",
      "attribution": "Mexican authorities and IMF Financial Soundness Indicators",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year financial-stability evidence through the second quarter.",
      "limitations": "Sector-level indicators do not establish regulatory enforcement against connected actors, household access to credit, or the ruler's personal contribution.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0008",
      "locator": "page 54",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005",
      "actor": "Mexico's financial system and sovereign market",
      "action": "experienced higher interest rates, sovereign yields, spreads, and private-sector credit growth in the first half of 2022",
      "mechanism": "financial-market pricing and financial-system lending",
      "outcome": "By June 2022, the period-average 28-day treasury auction rate was 6.4 percent, the ten-year local-currency sovereign yield was 8.4 percent, and the EMBIG spread was 380.9 basis points; projected financial-system credit growth to the nonfinancial private sector was 10.7 percent, while nonperforming loans were 2.3 percent.",
      "dates": "2022 through June for market and loan-quality indicators; some values are projections",
      "quantities": "Exchange rate 20.3 pesos per U.S. dollar; treasury rate 6.4%; EMBIG spread 380.9 basis points; ten-year yield 8.4%; private-sector credit growth 10.7%; NPL ratio 2.3%",
      "attribution": "Bank of Mexico, National Banking and Securities Commission, National Institute of Statistics and Geography, Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, and IMF staff estimates",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year financial-conditions context.",
      "limitations": "The series mix observed June data and projections and do not isolate policy causes.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0009",
      "locator": "page 54",
      "start_segment_id": "S00006",
      "end_segment_id": "S00011",
      "actor": "Mexico's external public and private sectors",
      "action": "maintained international reserves while carrying external debt and financing needs",
      "mechanism": "reserve accumulation, external borrowing, and debt service",
      "outcome": "In 2022, gross international reserves were reported at US$203.6 billion, equivalent to 3.9 months of imports, 284.2 percent of short-term debt, and 123.3 percent of the IMF reserve-adequacy metric. Projected gross external debt was 31.6 percent of GDP, including public external debt of 20.6 percent, and projected external debt service was 6.2 percent of GDP.",
      "dates": "2022; reserve level and GDP ratio include March or June observations, while several ratios and debt values are projections",
      "quantities": "Reserves US$203.6 billion; 3.9 months of imports; 284.2% of short-term debt; 123.3% of ARA metric; gross external debt 31.6% of GDP; public external debt 20.6%; private external debt 11.1%; debt service 6.2%",
      "attribution": "Bank of Mexico, National Banking and Securities Commission, National Institute of Statistics and Geography, Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, and IMF staff estimates",
      "period_fit": "Target-year evidence on external buffers and vulnerabilities.",
      "limitations": "Observed dates vary and several values are projections; reserve adequacy and debt ratios do not alone demonstrate policy quality or distribution.",
      "polarity": "mixed_positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0010",
      "locator": "page 55",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005",
      "actor": "Mexico's economy",
      "action": "grew in 2022 while experiencing high inflation and investment led primarily by the private sector",
      "mechanism": "consumption, investment, net exports, and price dynamics",
      "outcome": "IMF staff projected real GDP growth of 2.1 percent in 2022. Consumption contributed 4.5 percentage points and investment 1.0 point, while net exports subtracted 1.0 point. End-period inflation was projected at 8.5 percent and average inflation at 8.0 percent.",
      "dates": "2022 projection, with historical and medium-term comparison for 2019-2027",
      "quantities": "GDP growth 2.1%; consumption contribution 4.5 points; investment contribution 1.0 point; net-export contribution -1.0 point; end-period inflation 8.5%; average inflation 8.0%",
      "attribution": "Bank of Mexico, National Institute of Statistics and Geography, Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, Bloomberg, and IMF staff projections",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year macroeconomic outcome evidence.",
      "limitations": "The figures are projections and aggregate outcomes; they do not establish distribution, policy causality, or the ruler's individual role.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.4", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0011",
      "locator": "page 55",
      "start_segment_id": "S00008",
      "end_segment_id": "S00010",
      "actor": "Mexico's nonfinancial public sector and domestic economy",
      "action": "combined a fiscal deficit with investment and saving in 2022",
      "mechanism": "public finances and public-private capital formation",
      "outcome": "The nonfinancial public-sector overall balance was projected at negative 3.8 percent of GDP and the primary balance at positive 0.7 percent. Gross domestic investment was 21.0 percent of GDP, including public fixed investment of 2.8 percent and private fixed investment of 17.8 percent; gross domestic saving was 19.8 percent, with public saving negative 1.0 percent.",
      "dates": "2022 projection",
      "quantities": "Overall balance -3.8%; primary balance 0.7%; gross investment 21.0%; fixed investment 20.6%; public fixed investment 2.8%; private fixed investment 17.8%; gross saving 19.8%; public saving -1.0% of GDP",
      "attribution": "Bank of Mexico, National Institute of Statistics and Geography, Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, Bloomberg, and IMF staff projections",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year evidence on fiscal stance and capital formation.",
      "limitations": "The aggregate data do not identify investment quality, project delivery, procurement integrity, regional distribution, or causal attribution to the ruler.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0012",
      "locator": "page 56",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00012",
      "actor": "Mexico's banking system",
      "action": "expanded nominal private-sector credit and monetary liabilities in 2022",
      "mechanism": "bank lending and money creation",
      "outcome": "Credit to the private sector rose to 7.759 trillion pesos in 2022, while bank credit to the nonfinancial private sector grew 10.7 percent. However, such credit declined as a share of GDP from 26.7 percent in 2021 to 26.5 percent in 2022.",
      "dates": "2022 projection, compared with 2018-2021",
      "quantities": "Private-sector credit 7.759 trillion pesos; credit growth 10.7%; credit-to-GDP ratio 26.5%; broad-money growth 11.0%",
      "attribution": "Bank of Mexico, National Institute of Statistics and Geography, and IMF staff estimates",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year monetary and credit evidence.",
      "limitations": "The monetary-sector data follow IMF methodological criteria and may not coincide with Bank of Mexico definitions; aggregate credit does not establish access, competition, or distribution.",
      "polarity": "mixed_neutral",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.4", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0013",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "assessed Mexico's 2021 external position",
      "mechanism": "external-sector assessment against medium-term fundamentals and desirable policies",
      "outcome": "IMF staff judged the 2021 external position broadly consistent with fundamentals and desirable policies and attributed its rebalancing to domestic and foreign economic reopening, recovery, and a smaller fiscal-policy gap. Staff expected the current-account deficit to stabilize near 1 percent of GDP over the medium term.",
      "dates": "Assessment of 2021 with medium-term projection published in the 2022 report",
      "quantities": "Medium-term current-account deficit around 1% of GDP",
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Primarily a 2021 inherited-condition assessment available during the 2022 ruler-period; useful as immediate context but not a pure target-year outcome.",
      "limitations": "The assessment concerns the external position rather than broad welfare and does not isolate the ruler's contribution.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0014",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00005",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "identified structural reforms needed to raise Mexico's medium- and long-term growth and exports",
      "mechanism": "removing investment obstacles, reducing informality and governance gaps, increasing private energy participation, and reforming Pemex's strategy and governance",
      "outcome": "Staff characterized these reforms as critical for stronger growth, exports, and continued external sustainability, implying that unresolved investment, informality, governance, energy, and Pemex constraints remained.",
      "dates": "Policy assessment current to the 2022 consultation, with medium- and long-term horizon",
      "quantities": "none",
      "attribution": "IMF staff policy recommendation",
      "period_fit": "Directly relevant to policy conditions in the 2022 ruler-period, but it is a recommendation rather than evidence that reforms were enacted.",
      "limitations": "Normative recommendation; does not document government implementation or outcomes.",
      "polarity": "negative_limitation",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.4", "5B.5", "5B.6", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0015",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00008",
      "end_segment_id": "S00009",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "recommended continuation of the floating exchange-rate regime and constrained use of foreign-exchange intervention",
      "mechanism": "allowing the exchange rate to absorb shocks, limiting intervention to disorderly conditions, and retaining the IMF Flexible Credit Line as an added buffer",
      "outcome": "The recommended framework was intended to preserve external resilience against global tail risks.",
      "dates": "2022 policy assessment",
      "quantities": "none",
      "attribution": "IMF staff policy recommendation",
      "period_fit": "Current to the target year.",
      "limitations": "Recommendation rather than proof of the ruler's conduct; central-bank policy may reflect institutional independence rather than ruler control.",
      "polarity": "positive_if_implemented",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.3", "5B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0016",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00012",
      "end_segment_id": "S00015",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "assessed Mexico's external debt structure and foreign-exchange vulnerabilities",
      "mechanism": "local-currency denomination, corporate hedging, and exposure to foreign portfolio liabilities",
      "outcome": "Gross public external debt was estimated at 23 percent of GDP at end-2021, with roughly one-quarter held as local-currency government bonds. Staff considered the net international investment position sustainable and foreign-exchange risks reduced by local-currency denomination and corporate hedges, but identified large gross foreign portfolio liabilities as a vulnerability during global financial volatility.",
      "dates": "End-2021 assessment reported in 2022",
      "quantities": "Gross public external debt 23% of GDP; roughly one-quarter in holdings of local-currency government bonds",
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Immediate pre-target-year financial inheritance and vulnerability context.",
      "limitations": "Mainly end-2021 conditions; does not isolate actions taken during 2022.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0017",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00020",
      "end_segment_id": "S00025",
      "actor": "Mexico's economy and federal fuel-price policy",
      "action": "faced a projected widening of the current-account deficit during the 2022 commodity-price shock, while a domestic fuel-price ceiling and associated subsidies altered adjustment incentives",
      "mechanism": "higher global commodity prices affecting a net commodity importer, combined with fuel-price smoothing that weakened substitution and income responses",
      "outcome": "IMF staff projected the 2022 current-account deficit to increase to around 1 percent of GDP. Direct trade effects from the war in Ukraine were expected to be small because of limited regional trade links, but the fuel-price ceiling and subsidies were expected to amplify the commodity-price effect on the current account.",
      "dates": "2022 projection during the COVID-19 pandemic and war in Ukraine",
      "quantities": "Projected current-account deficit around 1% of GDP",
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year shock-response evidence.",
      "limitations": "The projection carried considerable uncertainty from the pandemic and war; the passage evaluates external-balance effects, not the subsidy policy's full welfare incidence.",
      "polarity": "negative_mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0018",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00039",
      "end_segment_id": "S00041",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "assessed Mexico's sovereign-debt, banking, corporate foreign-exchange, and capital-flow resilience",
      "mechanism": "long sovereign-debt maturity, local-currency denomination, bank resilience, and natural and financial corporate hedges",
      "outcome": "These features reduced government exposure to currency depreciation and refinancing risk and generally covered corporate foreign-exchange risk, but substantial foreign-investor participation left Mexico exposed to capital-flow reversals and higher risk premiums.",
      "dates": "2022 external-sector assessment",
      "quantities": "none",
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Current target-year resilience and vulnerability evidence.",
      "limitations": "Country-level assessment does not identify the ruler's specific contribution or whether resilience resulted from inherited institutions.",
      "polarity": "mixed_positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0019",
      "locator": "page 57",
      "start_segment_id": "S00042",
      "end_segment_id": "S00046",
      "actor": "Bank of Mexico and Mexican authorities",
      "action": "maintained a free-floating exchange rate, refrained from foreign-exchange intervention in 2021, and held reserves above the IMF adequacy benchmark",
      "mechanism": "central-bank exchange-rate policy, international reserves, the 2021 IMF SDR allocation, and the Flexible Credit Line",
      "outcome": "Gross reserves rose from US$199 billion at end-2020 to US$208 billion at end-2021, or 16 percent of GDP. At 131 percent of the IMF reserve-adequacy metric and 254 percent of short-term debt, IMF staff assessed reserves as adequate and regarded the Flexible Credit Line as an additional buffer.",
      "dates": "End-2020 to end-2021, assessed in the 2022 report",
      "quantities": "US$199 billion to US$208 billion; 16% of GDP; 131% of ARA metric; 254% of short-term debt; no FX intervention in 2021",
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment of Bank of Mexico and authority policies",
      "period_fit": "Immediate pre-target-year institutional and reserve position; relevant to 2022 shock capacity but not a direct 2022 action record.",
      "limitations": "Much of the reserve increase reflected the IMF general SDR allocation; central-bank conduct may be institutionally independent of the ruler.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0020",
      "locator": "page 58",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00003",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "identified commodity-price shocks as a high-likelihood, medium-impact risk and prescribed a monetary-policy response",
      "mechanism": "supply disruptions and demand shocks affecting retail fuel smoothing, fiscal expenditure, headline and core inflation, and inflation expectations",
      "outcome": "Staff advised monetary policy to respond if commodity shocks passed into core inflation and to keep inflation expectations anchored.",
      "dates": "Risk assessment current at the time of the 2022 consultation discussions",
      "quantities": "Likelihood classified high, corresponding under the matrix note to an assessed probability of 30-50 percent; impact classified medium",
      "attribution": "IMF staff Risk Assessment Matrix",
      "period_fit": "Direct target-year risk and recommended response, not evidence of actual implementation.",
      "limitations": "Subjective risk assessment; risks may interact and are not mutually exclusive.",
      "polarity": "risk_with_recommended_response",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0021",
      "locator": "page 58",
      "start_segment_id": "S00004",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "recommended a distributionally targeted response to inflation, falling incomes, inequality, and social-unrest risk",
      "mechanism": "tightening monetary policy, increasing and better targeting social transfers, accelerating investment in low-income regions, and avoiding continued fossil-fuel subsidies as a damaging populist response",
      "outcome": "The recommended measures were intended to relieve pressure on vulnerable households and address regional hardship while limiting inflation and economically damaging policy reactions.",
      "dates": "Risk assessment current at the time of the 2022 consultation discussions",
      "quantities": "Social-unrest likelihood classified high and impact on Mexico classified medium",
      "attribution": "IMF staff Risk Assessment Matrix",
      "period_fit": "Directly relevant to 2022 inflation and social-protection policy choices, but records recommendations rather than execution.",
      "limitations": "Subjective scenario assessment; does not establish that transfers were increased, properly targeted, or that regional investment was implemented.",
      "polarity": "negative_risk_with_recommended_response",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0022",
      "locator": "page 58",
      "start_segment_id": "S00008",
      "end_segment_id": "S00010",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "identified a high-likelihood risk that food and energy shocks could de-anchor inflation expectations and recommended decisive monetary tightening",
      "mechanism": "policy-rate restraint to counter pass-through from headline to core inflation and avert a wage-price spiral",
      "outcome": "Staff advised ensuring that the policy rate remained contractionary if upside inflation surprises caused medium- or long-term expectations to rise substantially.",
      "dates": "2022 risk assessment",
      "quantities": "Likelihood classified high; impact classified medium",
